what: Which clips the Tier 1 warm start helps, measured on the first seven that landed.
the_split: Every clip that gained ships its FINAL checkpoint. Every clip whose shipped checkpoint was picked EARLIER by the z-drop rule lost.
why_that_would_be: z-drop picking an earlier checkpoint is a statement that late-stage training made that clip worse. The fine-tune re-runs exactly that late stage -- 299,999,232 to 349,999,104 -- so on those clips it reproduces the degradation selection had rejected. e20 is the clearest: z-drop picked 300M over the 350M final, and fine-tuning from 300M to 350M took it from 0.715 to 0.480.
caveat: seven clips, one seed. The split is clean but it is a hypothesis, not a law.
action_taken: The three live boxes were re-queued onto their final-checkpoint clips only (e04 e06 e09 | e10 e12 e16 e17 e18 | e21 e22 e23 e26 e29), dropping 11 predicted-loss clips. Those clips cost about $4.80 and could not have changed the entry: the no-regression adoption rule rejects a regression, so a predicted loss contributes exactly nothing either way. The money buys information we already have.
